visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A young man with short dark hair wearing a bright yellow t-shirt sits at a wooden table in a dimly lit indoor room with beige walls. He holds a blue pen and writes intently on a notebook while looking down, occasionally looking up as if reciting something. (2) The scene shifts to a medium shot of a nameplate on a desk that reads 'Host: Ethan Kuan' in Traditional Chinese, next to a red coffee cup. The man is then shown in a black hair-cutting cape while a person off-camera massages his face and another adjusts his hair; he drinks from a dark canned beverage. (3) He is now in a large, brightly lit hall with a stage, wearing a crisp white button-down shirt. He holds a microphone with an orange foam cover, rehearsing movements on stage and interacting with staff members who are setting up banners and seating. (4) The final phase shows the actual event in progress. The man stands behind a podium with a 'World Obesity Day' logo, speaking into the microphone with a professional posture. He is joined by several older men in business suits on stage, participating in a ceremony where they place their hands on a large glowing sphere.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a male narrator's voice, characterized by high energy and clear articulation, explaining the duties of a press conference host. A light, upbeat acoustic guitar BGM plays at a moderate tempo in the background. (2) A transition is marked by a subtle whoosh effect as the narration continues, detailing preparations. The background music swells slightly during a montage of makeup sounds and muffled background chatter. (3) The vocal track shifts to include live audio from a rehearsal; the narrator's voice is heard through a PA system with a slight room reverb. A sharp ding sound effect signals the start of a specific rehearsal phase. (4) The final section features the narrator's professional hosting speech, with higher volume and authoritative tone. Sounds of crowd applause and mechanical clicks from cameras are audible, layered over the continuous upbeat BGM.
